technical_and_design_decisions: The Admin SPI will be defined as a Java interface module (spring-xd-admin-spi) with abstractions for ModuleStatus, ModuleDescriptor, and ModuleDescriptor.Key, placed in a shared module so it can be consumed by both client and server code.

A new module registry abstraction (ModuleRegistry) will sit on top of the Admin SPI, acting as a higher-level facade for discovery, status lookup, and bulk retrieval, so the SPI implementations remain thin adapters to the underlying system.

Two concrete Admin SPI implementations will be built: a Receptor implementation (delegating to the Receptor API used by Spring XD on CF) and a CloudController implementation (delegating to the CF Cloud Controller API). Both will live in a dedicated implementations package/module under the shared SPI repo.

Profile-based wiring (U5) will use Spring's @Profile annotations and dedicated application-{profile}.yml / property files so the correct SPI implementation is auto-selected when running as java -jar admin, cf push admin, or ltc create admin.

Eureka integration (U6/U8) will use spring-cloud-netflix-eureka-client; module instances will self-register on startup with metadata stored in the Eureka instance info map, and the ModuleRegistry will query Eureka for discovery and status.

Module search by name (U7) will be implemented both in the module registry (querying the registry's index) and via Eureka's lookup by app name (which is parameterized beyond the default spring.application.name).
Project will use Java 17 (per Spring 6.0 baseline), Maven for build, and existing Spring XD conventions for module packaging.
assumptions: A productive developer working full-time (8h/day) is assumed; 'workdays' map to 8 hours of focused development effort.
The Receptor and CloudController APIs are already accessible from the JVM (clients available or a thin HTTP client wrapper is acceptable); no new API design is required for them.
A Eureka server is assumed to be available in the target deployment environments (CF, ltc, standalone), and the Eureka client configuration (URL, credentials) is provided externally.
No major refactoring of existing Spring XD code is in scope — only additive changes for the SPI, registry, and Eureka integration.
The developer has working familiarity with Spring XD, Spring Cloud, and Cloud Foundry concepts; no learning/ramp-up time is included.
Unit tests target ~70% coverage of the new code; integration tests cover the three profile scenarios and Eureka round-trip flows.
Existing test infrastructure (CI, mock servers) can be reused; setting up new CI pipelines is out of scope.
Documentation is concise Javadoc plus a short README section; no separate user guide is required.

activities.activity_name: Create shared SPI module/repository and build setup (U3)
activities.activity_description: Create the new spring-xd-admin-spi Maven module, set up its pom, package structure, and wire it into the parent reactor build so SPI interfaces and implementations have a permanent home. Configure dependency management for shared libraries.

activities.activity_name: Design and implement Admin SPI interfaces
activities.activity_description: Define the ModuleStatus, ModuleDescriptor, ModuleDescriptor.Key types and the AdminSPI interface with getStatus(ModuleDescriptor), listModules(), and getAllStatuses() methods. Add Javadoc and base implementations where appropriate.

activities.activity_name: Design and implement Module Registry abstraction (U4)
activities.activity_description: Create the initial ModuleRegistry interface and a default in-memory implementation. Provide methods to register modules, look up by descriptor, list all, and search by name. This serves as the foundation that SPI implementations plug into.

Implement the AdminSPI backed by the Receptor API: translate Receptor responses to ModuleStatus/ModuleDescriptor, implement getStatus, listModules, and the bulk map method. Include client wiring and error handling.

Implement the AdminSPI backed by the CF Cloud Controller API: map app instances to ModuleStatus/ModuleDescriptor, implement the required methods, handle paging/authentication, and convert CF-specific errors into the SPI's exception model.

Add @Configuration classes annotated with @Profile to register the appropriate AdminSPI bean per profile (default for java -jar admin, cf for cf push admin, ltc for ltc create admin). Include property files and a profile-selection switch in the launcher.

Integrate spring-cloud-netflix-eureka-client into s-c-s modules so they self-register with Eureka on install/startup, exposing themselves for discovery via the Spring XD Admin SPI and Module Registry.

Extend Eureka registration so module metadata (group, index, deployment context, custom properties) is stored in the Eureka instance info metadata map, and implement the repository-side logic to read this metadata when determining state.

Add a findByName(String name) capability to the ModuleRegistry and a corresponding lookup path in the Admin SPI implementations so modules can be retrieved by a custom name independent of the default spring.application.name.

activities.activity_name: Unit tests for SPI, registry, and profile wiring
activities.activity_description: Write JUnit/Mockito unit tests for the AdminSPI interfaces, ModuleRegistry, Receptor/CloudController adapters, and profile-based bean selection. Cover happy paths, error mapping, and edge cases.

activities.activity_name: Integration tests for the three deployment profiles and Eureka flow
activities.activity_description: Build integration tests that exercise java -jar admin, cf push admin, and ltc create admin paths, plus Eureka registration/lookup round-trips against a test Eureka instance and stubbed Receptor/CloudController endpoints.
Write Javadoc for public APIs, a README section explaining the SPI, registry, profile wiring, and Eureka integration, plus a short upgrade note. Final code review fixes and cleanup.
